label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Good evening Mr Kehinde Ogunleye, my name is [Your Name]. I am the owner of the black Jansport bag you found on the bus on Friday, 6 November, from Oshodi to Igando. I believe you called the number on my lab manual, and I am very grateful you did that instead of throwing the bag away. Many people would not have done that, and I do not take it for granted.

I want to explain the situation honestly, because I do not want you to think I am taking advantage of your kindness. The bag contains my lab manual, dissecting kit, student ID card, two textbooks, my calculator and my glasses. My BIO 101 practical is on Wednesday, 11 November at 10 a.m., and the lab attendant is strict. Without the dissecting kit and my ID card, I will not be allowed to enter the hall, and I may have to repeat the practical. That is why I am trying so hard to get the bag back before then.

On the second call you said I should send 40k or forget the bag. I understand that you did not simply pick up an ordinary bag, and I respect that, but 40k is honestly more than I am able to do. Even the bag together with everything inside it is not worth that much, and the whole amount would be a serious strain on me.

What I can manage is 10k, which is my entire allowance, and I want you to also accept it as a thank you for the trouble and for returning my things. My roommate Adaeze has offered to come with me, and we can meet in the daytime at a public place so you are not at any disadvantage. Ikotun roundabout or the gate of the Ikotun police division would both be fine, whichever is easier for you. Please choose a day before Wednesday and a time that works, and I will come with the money and the bag will be in my hands within the hour.

Mr Kehinde, I am not a mugu, I am only a student who did not plan for this to happen. I am asking you to please help me, and I will make sure you are fully rewarded for your effort. I look forward to your reply.

Kind regards,
[Your Name]
[Your phone number]
